name: Price transparency list
status: Client review draft. Ranges transcribed from Elijah’s October 14, 2026, notes. Jesse and Elijah must review the exact scope and wording before publication.
inclusionsHeading: What your AC repair quote should explain.
inclusionsIntro: Before you approve a repair, ask which checks are included and what any extra work would cost.

groups.title: Check how the AC runs
items: Check that the thermostat calls for cooling
Check indoor blower operation
Check outdoor fan and equipment operation
Check the accessible filter and note airflow concerns
Check the repaired function after the work

groups.title: Look for related concerns
items: Check accessible wiring and connections
Check accessible cooling coils
Check visible refrigerant connections for concerns
Check accessible water drainage
Note unusual sounds and visible wear
Complete the applicable equipment safety checks
Explain anything we could not check and why

groups.title: Explain and complete the repair
items: Show you what supports the recommended repair
Explain the parts, labor, and full repair price
Tell you what the repair covers and leaves out
Get your approval before starting the repair or any additional work
Use compatible replacement parts when needed

groups.title: Help you know what comes next
items: Explain what was repaired and tested
Review any other findings from the inspection
Tell you what needs attention now and what can wait
Show relevant settings and care steps
Explain what to watch for if the problem returns
Leave a service record and a tidy work area

inclusionsLimit: The checks depend on your AC, its condition, and safe access. Confirm the inspection charge and which checks your visit includes. Any additional repair needs its own price and your approval.
examplesHeading: See the work behind an AC repair.
examplesIntro: A clear price starts with a clear repair. These examples show the work, a price range, and what can change the total. Ask for the full quote before approving work.
exampleLabel: Illustrative repair examples. Price ranges are from MGI’s October 14, 2026, service-manager notes. Your quote is based on your equipment and the work needed.

cases.title: A motor needs a new capacitor.
cases.finding: Example: testing finds a weak or failed capacitor, an electrical part that helps a motor run. A cooling problem can have more than one cause.
work: Check the capacitor test result and explain why replacement is recommended
Match the replacement to the equipment’s required size and rating
Remove the capacitor being replaced
Supply a compatible replacement capacitor
Install the new part and reconnect its wiring
Test the replacement capacitor
Check how the equipment runs after replacement
Explain any separate cooling concern found during the checks
cases.driver: Capacitor type, access, and any separate electrical problem can change the price.
cases.limit: Confirm whether this range applies to your single-run or dual capacitor. Ask whether diagnosis, tax, or an after-hours charge is separate. Motor or refrigerant repairs need their own quote.
cases.priceBasis: One capacitor replacement with a compatible part and an operating check.

priceSource.approval: Final scope and public wording pending Jesse and Elijah review

cases.title: The indoor fan needs a conventional original-equipment motor.
cases.finding: Example: the blower motor needs replacement. It runs the fan that moves cooled air through your home. This range is for a conventional original-equipment motor that uses a capacitor.
work: Confirm which replacement motor fits the equipment
Remove the existing blower motor
Supply and install the compatible replacement motor
Check the capacitor size required by the new motor
Change the capacitor if the replacement motor requires it
Reconnect the motor’s wiring
Test operation and measure the motor’s electrical draw
Explain any other finding that needs separate work
cases.driver: Motor type, access, matching parts, and separate control or airflow problems can change the total.
cases.limit: The quote must identify whether a matching capacitor is included and whether diagnosis and tax are separate. Electronically controlled, variable-speed, and universal motors are outside this range. Refrigerant work needs its own quote.
cases.priceBasis: Conventional original-equipment blower motor (OEM PSC). Other motor types have different ranges.

priceSource.approval: Final scope and public wording pending Jesse and Elijah review

cases.title: An indoor cooling coil out of warranty needs replacement.
cases.finding: Example: the repair calls for a new indoor coil, where refrigerant takes heat out of the air. The parts connected around it can change the work.
work: Confirm the replacement coil and the work listed in the quote
Complete the refrigerant recovery needed for coil removal
Remove the existing indoor coil
Install the selected replacement coil
Adjust the connected air box if included in the quote
Complete any quoted intake, exhaust, or humidifier connection changes
Connect the refrigerant lines as listed in the scope
Complete the quoted refrigerant and operating checks
Explain the checks completed and any remaining work
cases.driver: Coil size, access, refrigerant type and amount, and changes to surrounding connections can change the price.
cases.limit: Ask which connection work, refrigerant, and operating checks are included, and whether diagnosis and tax are separate. A coil with parts-warranty coverage needs a separate quote. Other cooling problems are separate work.
cases.priceBasis: Indoor cooling coil replacement without parts-warranty coverage, for the work listed in your quote.

priceSource.approval: Final scope and public wording pending Jesse and Elijah review

basis: Before you decide, get a quote that lists the work, the full price, and whether visit fees, tax, refrigerant, or permit costs are included or separate. Any additional work needs its own price and your approval.
